judgment: A coherent dimensional scene could integrate companions better. Studio-like polish alone adds no personal distinctiveness; the original moth and its curious making must remain the source of identity.
guardrails: Keep graphic oval eyes, small mouth, unequal paddle antennae and green wing markings. Add soft matte volume, lighting and four-wing separation. Preserve tiny mittens, attached stub feet and compact proportions; avoid generic plush-toy anatomy, realistic insect texture or enlarged human eyes. All three moths remain the same character.
cameos: Exactly two, one quiet group behind the rear workshop watching the same activity; zero fallback. Foreground bench, coding moth, MacBook and path stay exclusive. Cameos remain optional scene content, never the permanent identity.
revision: Where feasible compare matched 3D versions with zero and two cameos; a painted baseline alone cannot separate the new rendering style from added-cast value.
failure: Reject if the moth no longer reads as the same character as the graphic avatar, or companion colour/contrast competes with the coder at GitHub size.
evidence: Proposal read. Actual park and picnic reference inspection reused from this conversation; refined V5 mascot reference freshly viewed.
skills: Full prior emil-design-eng, choreograph and design-taste-frontend readings reused: hierarchy, shared intention, coherent identity. UI-motion prescriptions do not apply.
limits: No rendered 3D variation, human recognition evidence, score or artwork/publication approval.
pair: Read A after saving. Confirm same scoped test; add matched 3D zero-cameo comparison to distinguish styling from cast value.
